title: Permissions & Settings

body.text: Control what Claude can do with
permission rules: allow (do it directly), ask (ask first), deny (never)
— set them in settings.json at the user level (all projects) or the project level (shared by the team).

example: "allow: ['Bash(npm *)', 'Bash(git status)'] / deny: ['Bash(rm -rf *)'] — npm runs directly, rm -rf is blocked"

title: Set permissions to fit the work

body.text: start strict and loosen — allow only the frequently-used, safe commands
— like tests/lint/build can be allowed, while git push, deleting files, and touching the database should always ask.

example: "The team sets in .claude/settings.json: tests and lint auto-run, but deploy requires a person to confirm every time"

question: What are the three permission levels?
What commands are appropriate to auto-allow?

options.text: Tests, lint, build — safe and frequently used

question: What's the benefit of project-level settings?

options.text: The team uses one shared rule set across the project

question: How should you set permissions well?

options.text: Grant permissions that fit the work — not too much or too little
